taramandal.intro: Taramandal is different from Navtara. Every nakshatra belongs to one or more constellation groups, and planets placed in a group take on that mandal’s cosmic role.

taramandal.notNavtaraBody: Navtara counts nine tara steps outward from the birth star. Taramandal works differently: fixed constellation groups that each hold nakshatras as members. When planets fall within a mandal, what they signify takes on that group’s cosmic energy — which can produce patterns sometimes mistaken for stelliums.
taramandal.coverageBody: The only remaining gaps are the upcoming Mrityu Karma and Gyan mandals (their kings are recorded; the full groups are pending). Partial members in other mandals still count.

special.title: Navatara and nadi nakshatras
special.lead: Counting from the janma star, the 27 stars fall into three rounds (paryay) of nine taras. Certain counts carry a fixed role of their own — career, mother, father, mind, ruin, rise — so the planets sitting there, and the transits passing over them, speak to that part of life.
special.povNote: Janma star: {star} ({lord}). The Moon is the main point of view; Lagna, Sun and the running mahadasha lord add further layers.
special.gridCaption: Rows are the nine taras, columns the three rounds. Stars sharing a row share a lord and play the same tara role. Named cells are nadi roles; codes show this chart's planets.

taraEffect.Janma: Tied to body, health and temperament; malefics here weigh on wellbeing, benefics lift it.
taraEffect.Sampat: Brings resources and prosperity in its periods; a malefic here can still feel a sense of lack.
taraEffect.Vipat: Loses some strength; its houses and significations meet setbacks and poor choices.
taraEffect.Kshema: Supported and protected; its significations prosper in its periods.
taraEffect.Pratyari: Meets blocks in what it signifies and rules; can strain health in its periods.
taraEffect.Sadhaka: Helps achievement; ambitions linked to it tend to be realised.
taraEffect.Vadha: Difficult; can bring sudden, eighth-house-like turns in its periods.
taraEffect.Mitra: Friendly and helpful to the chart's progress.
taraEffect.AtiMitra: A strong ally; supportive in every way.

janma.name: Janma
janma.meaning: Body, health and the self. What touches this star touches you directly.

jati.name: Jati
jati.meaning: Lineage, community and the society that supports you. A favourable star for family continuity and comfort.

matru.name: Matru
matru.meaning: The mother and the bond with her. Malefics here or transiting it affect her and the relationship.

karma.name: Karma
karma.meaning: Work, career and reputation. Planets here colour the profession; good transits can lift the career.

sanghatika.name: Sanghatika
sanghatika.meaning: Close associations that can wound. Planets here suffer through company and intimate ties.

samudaya.name: Samudaya
samudaya.meaning: Rise and good karma carried from the past. Planets here help you ascend in their periods.

adhana.name: Adhana
adhana.meaning: Conception and creativity — where new projects are seeded. The father is also judged from here.

vainashika.name: Vainashika
vainashika.meaning: Ruin and loss. Planets here are weakened; watch health, and avoid starting important work when the Moon is here.

manasa.name: Manasa
manasa.meaning: The mind. Malefics here or transiting it bring worry and unclear decisions; Saturn's entry here is often felt like the start of Sade Sati.

abhisheka.name: Abhisheka
abhisheka.meaning: Coronation — power, status and achievement. Benefic transits here raise standing and open doors.

degrees.title: Sensitive degrees
degrees.lead: The exact degree inside a star can matter as much as the star itself. These checks flag knots, blessed degrees, danger degrees and star edges.

explain.gandanta: Gandanta: the knot where a water sign ends and a fire sign begins (Revati–Ashwini, Ashlesha–Magha, Jyeshtha–Mula). It brings karmic intensity and turning points.
explain.pushkaraNavamsha: Pushkara Navamsha: a nourishing navamsha that strengthens and protects the planet.
explain.pushkaraBhaga: Pushkara Bhaga: the single most auspicious degree of the sign (within 1°).
explain.mrityuBhaga: Mrityu Bhaga: a classical danger degree. Read it as a point of strain and transformation, never on its own as a verdict.
explain.sandhi: Nakshatra sandhi: within 0.5° of a star boundary. A small error in birth time can move the planet into the next star, so check the time before relying on its star.

gandmool.title: Gandmool dosha
gandmool.lead: A child born with the Moon in Ashwini, Ashlesha, Magha, Jyeshtha, Mula or Revati is called Gandmool. These stars sit where a water sign ends and a fire sign begins, and each pada is said to affect a particular person or area of life.

gandmool.strongNote: This pada touches the water–fire junction (Gandanta), so tradition treats it as the strongest form.
gandmool.abhuktaNote: The Moon is within the last or first moments of Jyeshtha–Mula (Abhukta Mula), the most sensitive part of Gandmool.
gandmool.clear: Not Gandmool: the birth Moon is in {star}.

gandmool.remedyCharity: Charity and feeding of Brahmins or the needy on the day of the Shanti.
gandmool.tableCaption: What each pada of the six Gandmool stars is said to affect. Rose cells are difficult, teal ones favourable; the dashed outline marks the strong junction pada. Your pada is outlined in gold.
gandmool.note: Traditions differ on some pada effects. Gandmool is one factor and is read together with the whole chart, never on its own.

yogi.title: Yogi and Avayogi stars
yogi.lead: The Yogi point (Sun + Moon + 93°20') falls in a star whose lord, the Yogi, brings wealth and ease. The point 186°40' later marks the Avayogi, whose lord works against prosperity. Planets in their stars, or ruled by them, carry that influence.
yogi.note: Strengthen the Yogi graha; its periods and the planets in its stars tend to bring prosperity. Periods of the Avayogi call for care with money.

kota.title: Kota Chakra — the fortress
kota.lead: Your birth star stands at the north-east gate of a fort with four walls: Stambha (the core), Madhya, Prakara and Bahya (outside). Each side holds seven of the 28 stars, Abhijit included. Planets move in through a corner (NE, SE, SW, NW) toward the core and out toward a cardinal point (E, S, W, N). Malefics coming in or sitting in the core threaten the fort; benefics coming in defend it.
kota.transitGold: Transit and chosen-time readings of the fort are a Gold feature; the birth positions are shown.
kota.failed: Could not load today's transits; the birth positions are shown.

verdictText.bhanga: Malefics are moving in while benefics are moving out. Tradition reads this as a time of setbacks, illness or disputes; check it against the running dasha.
verdictText.vijaya: Benefics are moving in and malefics are leaving. Tradition reads this as protection and success in contests.
verdictText.mixed: Neither the breach nor the victory pattern is complete. Read individual planets below.

kota.swamiInside: Kota Swami {swami} sits in the {layer} (Madhya or Stambha), where the lord of the fort should be — a sign of strength.
kota.swamiOutside: Kota Swami {swami} is in the {layer}, away from the Madhya and Stambha where the lord of the fort should sit.
kota.palaOnWall: Kota Pala {pala} (Moon pada {pada}) stands on the Prakara, where the guard should be.
kota.palaInside: Kota Pala {pala} (Moon pada {pada}) has come inside to the {layer} — the guard has left the wall.
kota.palaElsewhere: Kota Pala {pala} (Moon pada {pada}) is in the {layer}, not on the Prakara guard wall.
kota.invertedSeats: Seats are inverted: the Swami is outside the palace while the Pala sits inside. Tradition reads this as weak protection — carelessness with medicine, diet, or risky choices can add harm. This is a classical caution, not a medical diagnosis.
kota.dualRoleOk: {planet} is both Kota Swami and Kota Pala, and sits in the {layer} — a natural fit for its nature.
kota.dualRoleOff: {planet} is both Kota Swami and Kota Pala, but sits in the {layer}. A natural malefic prefers the Prakara or Bahya; a natural benefic prefers the Madhya or Stambha.

twelfth.twelfthLord: Running dasha of {list} (lord of the 12th from the Moon) sharpens the fort's stress toward loss, hospitalisation, or drain — weigh it with the dasha, not alone.
twelfth.inTwelfth: Running dasha of {list}, sitting in the 12th from the Moon, sharpens the fort's stress toward loss or bodily strain — weigh it with the dasha, not alone.
twelfth.both: Running dasha of {list} ties to the 12th from the Moon (lord {lord} and/or occupant), sharpening the fort's stress — weigh it with the dasha, not alone.

kota.fortCaption: Drawn the traditional way, with East on top and the birth star ({star}) at the top-left (north-east) gate, ringed in gold. Coloured dots are planets: rose for danger, amber for caution, teal for support.
kota.note: Kota Swami is the lord of the Moon's sign. Kota Pala is the Avakahada letter-class lord of the Moon's pada (Abhijit → Venus; Ketu never guards). Prefer the Swami in Madhya or Stambha and the Pala on the Prakara. Today's view uses mean Rahu and Ketu, always retrograde; their entering and leaving are swapped, as for any retrograde planet. Like any transit, the fort's reading works within the running dasha.
kota.birthNote: Your birth planets placed in the fort. Malefics deep inside at birth show lasting weak points that tend to surface in their own dashas; the breach or victory verdict is read from transits. Kota Swami is {swami}; Kota Pala is {pala} (Moon pada {pada}).

journey.title: The life journey through the 27 stars
journey.intro: A sign is a broad brush. Aquarius, for example, holds parts of Dhanishta, Shatabhisha and Purva Bhadrapada, three stars with very different natures, so a reading built on the sign alone stays general. The nakshatra gives the specific picture.
journey.lead: One traditional way to read the 27 stars in order is as a lifetime, from the first breath in Ashwini to release in Revati. Planets placed in a star show which stage's lessons are active in this chart.
journey.pathCaption: Read left to right, then back, then forward again. The birth star is ringed in gold; this chart's planets and Lagna sit above their stars. Select any star to read its stage.
journey.yourLead: The stages your planets and Lagna sit in, in path order. These are the themes this chart keeps returning to.
journey.note: This is a symbolic reading of the sequence, not a timetable: the stages describe themes, and a person meets them in their own order and time.

0.title: First breath
0.text: Life begins on pure instinct. We are carried entirely by others and act by reflex, quick and unthinking.

1.title: Holding on
1.text: The infant body changes fast. The first wants and refusals appear, and with them the first effort to feed ourselves.

2.title: First lessons
2.text: Walking, speaking and letters. Discipline trims raw instinct so that learning can take shape.

3.title: Taste of the world
3.text: New skills turn into enjoyment. The material world becomes attractive, fertile and full of things to grow.

4.title: Curiosity
4.text: The search begins. We follow whatever catches our interest, wandering from one discovery to the next.

5.title: Making sense
5.text: Experience has to be analysed, sometimes painfully, until it is understood. Storms clear the air.

6.title: Belonging
6.text: Feelings awaken. We find our place in family and community, mixing play with care for others.

7.title: Promise
7.text: Responsibility grows and life looks full of promise. The heart opens and nourishes what it loves.

8.title: Hard truths
8.text: The world shows its harsher side. Innocence ends, and we learn to manoeuvre, defend and survive.

9.title: Identity
9.text: A clear identity takes shape, together with a sense of roots, lineage and what we inherit.

10.title: Pleasure and partnership
10.text: With identity secure, we relax, create and enjoy. The search for a partner begins.

11.title: Commitment
11.text: Family, marriage and a steady role in society. Social identity grows alongside the personal one.

12.title: Skill at work
12.text: Worldly duties absorb us. We plan, organise and start projects with cleverness and dexterity.

13.title: Making
13.text: Plans become finished works. Craft, design and the pleasure of building something real.

14.title: Trade
14.text: What we made goes out into the world. We relate to others through exchange, independence and business.

15.title: A higher aim
15.text: Success leaves a hunger for something more meaningful. Purpose narrows to a single goal.

16.title: Devotion
16.text: That hunger is met through friendship, devotion and understanding the quiet laws of nature.

17.title: Seniority
17.text: We become the respected elder and protector, and must watch the pride that comes with the role.

18.title: Uprooting
18.text: What was built is pulled up to reveal what still remains to be understood. The impersonal begins here.

19.title: Invincibility
19.text: Having survived the uprooting, we feel unbeatable and start to share what we learned, still in our own way.

20.title: Larger purpose
20.text: Personal ambition is placed in service of something larger. Victory now means victory for all.

21.title: Listening
21.text: With the ego quieter, subtler and deeper voices can be heard. Learning comes through listening.

22.title: Rhythm
22.text: Living in step with that larger rhythm brings abundance, fame and fulfilment on every level.

23.title: The question
23.text: Even abundance is not enough. We turn inward and ask what existence itself is.

24.title: Austerity
24.text: The question drives intense sacrifice and discipline, willing to give up everything for truth.

25.title: The middle path
25.text: Wisdom arrives through calm, steady and gentler means. Depth replaces extremes.

26.title: Release
26.text: Every duality dissolves into the ocean of consciousness. The journey completes, and a new one can begin.
